bayts.text: Bring about for me today a victory – mighty is my Lord! – and lift the veils from me; grant me the (wondrous) signs.
O Accepter of repentance (At-Tawwāb), forgive me my sins and erase from me every idle word, and be for me in my world and in my Hereafter.
By Your being the One, the Subduer (Al-Wāḥid al-Qahhār), tame the enemies for me, O my Lord, and make my glad tiding everlasting in You.
You are the God Who exalts and raises whom You will: so make my life good in You.
Yours are the sky, the earths and the air together: guard me from the harm of all, and make my distinctions everlasting.
Yours are all the sultans, and likewise the kings and their followers: tame them for me before my meeting (with them).
Grant me constancy in what You are pleased with of deed, word and creed, at my dwelling.
Yours are all creatures and the lands: so be for me, O my God, in my abode and in my Ṭūbā (Touba).
Aid my precinct and my fortress; make my life good for me with what You love, and perfect in You my God-fearing.
I have been enriched by the One, the Subduer, (made free) of the throngs; He has been for me and repelled my poverty and my trial.
To Him I have turned, full of gratitude to Him for ever, and I hope from Him what none of my peers has attained.
By Your being the Powerful, the Subduer, the All-Capable, I hope for the constancy of what I love, in the place of my safety.
I have called on Him intimately, hoping He will not disappoint me and will turn toward me what surpasses my safety.
I have resolved to please Him as those who are righteous please Him, after my return to my family and my dwelling.
You are the All-Powerful (Al-Qadīr) by Whose power I hope to attain mastery: increase me beyond my good.
I have cast away what I had: lead to me, by Your being (God), in this world and the Other, what You are pleased with according to my desire.
Prolong my sojourn with acts of obedience made pure, and decree by Your dominion, O my Lord, my victory.
Turn toward me, by Your might, a might through which I may be a glorious servant, and make my favour from You everlasting.
You have trained me through enemies: tame them all for me, lead me to the beloved ones, and praise, Lord, my striving.
Lead to me for ever what surpasses wishes, out of generosity, and make Your Book, in the two Abodes, my pasture.
Lead to me always the cups of the (spiritual) folk, to quench me; give me to drink and make great, Lord, my draught.
O Lord of permanence, Who made my life endure for me, (making me) a servant, a server, blessed: protect my desire.
To You I have turned my face, calling on You, O my King: so answer, out of generosity, O Lord, my supplication.
You have saved me: so increase me, Lord, in salvation; protect me and protect what my dwelling holds.
You saved me yesterday from my return to (worldly) merchandise: so today be for me and make great from You my benefit.
You are the Preserver (Al-Ḥafīẓ) Whose protection I seek: so be my Preserver and increase, O Lord, my God-fearing.
To You is my turning as gain: lead my reins, O Lord, and grant me praise, Lord, for my night journey.
To You is my departure, now under way: lead my aim to me soon, (bringing me) back, and protect my course.
Grant me, by Your being the Bestower (Al-Wahhāb) without cause, what surpasses my expectation, and fill, Lord, my resting-place.
Lead this with kindness and generosity, and spare me slips: to You is my end, my God, from You my beginning.
I turned my face to You on a Saturday, in Rajab, and on a Tuesday, in Shaʿbān, (toward) my refuge.
O Lord, bless with peace my support, Muḥammad, and through him lead me to my hopes.
O Lord, bless him with peace beyond number, with the Family and the Companions, my salvation.
Upon him pour blessing and peace, with all, and be the One Who through me illumines my times and my places of safety.
Increase me in sciences with an unveiling that never leaves me, O You to Whom I complain: remove the cause of my complaint.
O best Enricher, Who fulfilled my needs without burdens, O You through Whose being for me I parted from my trial.
I have adorned the poems for you, thanking you: through them and through you they brought me unveiling and signs.
